solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hack can barely trip up right-wing group

indicators.note: to hack something is to chop it roughly about, so the words that follow are cut up and rearranged

blocks.note: all fifteen letters of these three words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A clumsy journalist can hardly avoid stumbling over a conservative political faction.
explanation.walkthrough: The REPUBLICAN PARTY is the right-of-centre US party, the GOP.
explanation.definitionFit: The Republicans are the conservative major party in American politics, so they are a right-leaning political organisation.

clue.text: Get to do a sermon after priest does one

indicators.note: 'does one' is slang for running off, so the named letter leaves the word

blocks.note: to deliver a sermon is to preach
P is the abbreviation for priest

explanation.surface: A curate must give a sermon once the vicar has scarpered.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove P from PREACH to leave REACH; 'does one' is British slang for leaving in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach a place is to arrive at it, a straightforward synonym for getting there.

clue.text: One who sees new reprieve will protect Conservative

indicators.note: something new has been made afresh, so the letters of the following word are remade in another order
to protect is to surround and shield, so one set of letters wraps round the other

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A political observer notes that a fresh stay of execution will shield a Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: To perceive is to notice or see, so a perceiver is a person who observes.

clue.text: Prison? That could be a lark!

blocks.note: first meaning: British slang for a prison sentence
second meaning: a lark is a songbird

explanation.surface: Someone jokes that a spell inside could be a bit of fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lark' looks like a romp or prank, which makes prison sound jolly; here it is the bird. Doing BIRD is British slang for serving time.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is British slang for jail time and also the general term for a feathered animal such as the lark.

clue.text: Beg for tales of mischievous sprites?

blocks.note: an imp is a mischievous little sprite
lore is a body of traditional stories

explanation.surface: A question asking whether someone pleads to hear stories of naughty fairies.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is read in reverse: 'tales of mischievous sprites' is imp lore, put together as IMP + LORE.
explanation.definitionFit: To implore is to plead earnestly, so it means to beg for something.

clue.text: A northern choir shunning university hosts

indicators.note: shunning means avoiding, so the named letter is kept out of the word

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for northern
a choir is a chorus
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A choir from the north stays away from a college that is hosting events.
explanation.walkthrough: The choir must first become its longer synonym before the university letter can be dropped from it.
explanation.definitionFit: News anchors are the presenters who front broadcasts, so they are programme hosts.

clue.text: Film studio stage on which a charge is set up

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means placed upwards, so the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a rap is a criminal charge, as in beat the rap
to stage a play is to mount it

explanation.surface: A movie company puts on a production with an accusation hanging over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage' is a verb, to put on a show; in a down entry the turned charge sits on top of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramount Pictures is one of the major Hollywood movie studios.

clue.text: Bit of bother with work round North Island

indicators.note: round means encircling, so one word goes about the other

blocks.note: a machine that works is said to run
N for North and I for Island

explanation.surface: A spot of trouble at the office around New Zealand's northern island.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-in is a quarrel or brush with someone, a minor spot of trouble.

clue.text: Long drink for a lady dancing with energy

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and change places, so they come out in another order

blocks.note: the fodder, letter for letter
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone orders a tall drink for a woman who is lively on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: A YARD OF ALE is a metre-long glass of beer traditionally downed in one as a pub challenge.
explanation.definitionFit: The yard glass is about three feet tall, so its beer is literally a lengthy drink.

clue.text: Heaven-sent supply of gas medic opens, perhaps, at the front

indicators.note: at the front points to the leading letter of each of the words just before it

blocks.note: air is a gas, or mix of gases
DR is the abbreviation for doctor
the initial letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A doctor turns on the oxygen supply, perhaps at the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heaven-sent' is a playful way of saying the supply drops from the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: An airdrop delivers supplies by parachute from an aircraft, so they literally come down from above.

clue.text: Angle to trap old and stiff examiner

indicators.note: to trap something is to hold it inside, so one word encloses another

blocks.note: a corner is an angle
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A rigid inspector tries to corner an elderly person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stiff' looks like an adjective for a strict examiner, but it is slang for a corpse.
explanation.definitionFit: A coroner investigates sudden deaths, so is the official who examines a dead body.

clue.text: Pay attention to editor, the guy's head here

indicators.note: the guy's head here means the man's word is placed at the top, before the other piece

blocks.note: the pronoun for a man
ED is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: Listen to the editor: the man in charge is right here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like the boss of the newspaper; it is a positional instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To heed advice is to take notice of it and act on it.

clue.text: Eschew one's bloomers and possibly start over

blocks.note: Go! is a command to start, and 'possibly' marks it as one example of a command
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Advice to skip the underwear and begin the day afresh.
explanation.walkthrough: The parsing is loose: 'start' is read as the word GO, which is a COMMAND, then O for over. Bloomers are old-fashioned women's knickers.
explanation.definitionFit: To go commando is the idiom for wearing no underpants, so it means doing without knickers.

clue.text: Hurtful rhyme that commercial starts off

indicators.note: starts off says the commercial's word comes at the very beginning of the rhyme's word

blocks.note: an ad is a commercial
verse is rhyme

explanation.surface: A jingle that opens a television advert causes offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverse means harmful or unfavourable, as in adverse effects.

clue.text: Witness a time trial getting on top of soldier

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time
a test is a trial
a soldier ant is a kind of ant

explanation.surface: An observer sees a timed race beating a serviceman.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'getting on top of' means the first pieces sit above ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: An attestant is someone who attests, that is, bears witness to a fact or signature.

clue.text: Moderation and discipline seen in others

indicators.note: something seen in a place sits inside it, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: the rest are the others
to train is to discipline

explanation.surface: Self-control and good conduct are qualities you notice in other people.
explanation.definitionFit: Restraint is holding oneself back, which is the same idea as temperance or self-control.

clue.text: Shrimp old writer caught in South Africa

indicators.note: a thing caught in something is held inside it

blocks.note: SA is the abbreviation for South Africa
a quill is a feather pen used in earlier times

explanation.surface: A small man, once an author, was arrested in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shrimp' tempts as a slur for a small person; it is the sea creature. 'Old writer' is a pen, not an author.
explanation.definitionFit: Squilla is a genus of mantis shrimps, burrowing marine crustaceans.

clue.text: Exotic lap dances could create a scene

indicators.note: exotic means outlandish and unfamiliar, so the letters take on a strange new order

blocks.note: the fodder, letter for letter

explanation.surface: Racy dancing in a club might cause a public fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Create a scene' sounds like causing a commotion; here a scene is a view.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape is a stretch of scenery, or a painting of one, so it is a view or scene.

clue.text: Soprano's happy after performer arrives

indicators.note: after says the soprano and happy pieces follow the performer rather than lead

blocks.note: a turn is a variety act or performer
S is the abbreviation for soprano
feeling up is feeling cheerful

explanation.surface: The singer is delighted once the act finally shows up.
explanation.walkthrough: A turn is a British music-hall or variety act, so 'performer' is the act itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn up is the everyday phrasal verb for appearing or getting somewhere.

clue.text: Artist holding dope is very good company

indicators.note: holding means gripping within, so one word goes inside another

blocks.note: PI is short for pious, a crossword stock for very good
CO is the abbreviation for company
a dope and an ass are both fools

explanation.surface: A painter carrying drugs is welcome among friends.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'dope' as drugs; here it is a fool. PI for pious is a stock crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Picasso was the Spanish painter who co-founded Cubism.

clue.text: Stated where one sees circus performers of extreme strength

indicators.note: stated means said out loud, so the answer is a word with the same sound

blocks.note: circus acts perform under canvas big tops

explanation.surface: Someone describes the venue for circus acts as remarkably powerful.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense means existing in a high degree, very strong or concentrated.

clue.text: Quarantine one very out of breath?

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
so means very, as in so tired
breathless for good means dead, and the late are the dead

explanation.surface: Someone panting heavily is asked whether they should be kept apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of breath' suggests panting; read as permanently out of breath it means dead, hence LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To quarantine people is to keep them apart from others to stop infection, that is, to separate them.

clue.text: Might I remove coach overturned by farm vehicle

indicators.note: something overturned is upended, so its letters run backwards

blocks.note: a coach is a bus
a tractor is a farm vehicle

explanation.surface: A worried driver wonders about clearing a coach knocked over by a tractor.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer speaking: a subtractor is one who takes away. The blogger notes it would read better with a question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A subtractor is something that takes a quantity away, so it would naturally ask whether it might deduct.

clue.text: Hopeless chess player

blocks.note: first meaning: a bleak, gloomy outlook
second meaning: the side with the dark pieces

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on a poor chess player.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a dismal, despairing outlook and also the player who moves second in chess.

clue.text: I very much doubt it is receding in a female

indicators.note: receding means going back, so the short word is read backwards
in places one set of letters inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A sceptic doubts a woman's hairline is retreating.
explanation.definitionFit: As if! is the scornful exclamation meaning that something is most unlikely.

clue.text: They're little nippers, but sound 27-ish essentially!

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so the centre letter is kept
sound means as heard, so the letters are what the result says aloud

blocks.note: the answer to 27 across means to run away
the middle letter of this suffix

explanation.surface: Biting insects that behave like they are running off.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 across means to flee; FLEE plus the S at the heart of 'ish' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleas are tiny biting insects, so they nip people and pets.

clue.text: Almost dark soon

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is lopped off

blocks.note: night is the dark part of the day

explanation.surface: Nightfall is coming shortly.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigh is an old word for near, so in time it means close at hand or shortly.

clue.text: A good parting farewell for 18 slow songs

indicators.note: parting means splitting open, so the farewell word is divided to admit other letters

blocks.note: adios is Spanish for goodbye, fitting for 18, the Spaniard Picasso
taken as written
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A fond goodbye to the painter is marked with gentle music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For 18' points to Picasso, a Spaniard, so the farewell is in Spanish.
explanation.definitionFit: Adagio is the musical term for a slow tempo, so adagios are slow pieces or movements.

clue.text: Worry consumed a contemptible type initially

indicators.note: initially means at the beginning, so the contemptible type's phrase is placed before the eating word

blocks.note: taken as written
git is British slang for an unpleasant or stupid person
to have consumed food is to have eaten it

explanation.surface: Anxiety ate away at a nasty person from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is read backwards from the surface: 'a contemptible type' comes first, then 'consumed'.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate is to make someone anxious or troubled, a synonym for the verb fret.

clue.text: Begin to dig footwear you bought for Bolt?

definitions.text: Begin to dig footwear you bought

blocks.clueFragment: Begin to dig footwear you bought
blocks.note: first meaning, read literally: to start liking the high shoes you purchased
second meaning: to run off, with a nod to the sprinter Usain Bolt

explanation.surface: A question whether the sprinter Bolt has come to love his new shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dig' is slang for like, and 'take to' means start liking. Usain Bolt is the record-holding Jamaican sprinter, but here bolt is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To take to one's heels is the idiom for running away, the same as to bolt.
